QUERY_PARAMETERS_INVALID: Query parameters do not match the registered schema. Fix: send only declared parameters with the required types. Example: send a JSON integer for an integer parameter.
QUERY_PARAMETERS_LIMIT: Query parameters exceed the configured size or complexity limit. Fix: reduce the parameter payload. Example: send a shorter list of filter values.
QUERY_PARAMETER_BINDING_INVALID: A registered YAML parameter could not bind to a supported query value. Fix: check the host template and parameter model. Example: bind a declared integer parameter to a numeric predicate value.
QUERY_NATIVE_INPUT_INVALID: A projected field does not have a supported scalar type. Fix: select a scalar JSON Pointer in the host definition. Example: project /reading/value for a numeric leaf.
QUERY_NATIVE_RESULT_INVALID: The transformation result does not match the registered output schema or JSON value contract. Fix: return a DataFrame with the declared columns and types. Example: cast a count column to Int64 when its declared type is integer.
QUERY_NATIVE_ISOLATION_INVALID: The isolated transformation or its parameter model is unavailable in the host configuration. Fix: use importable module-level definitions and register the transformation in the host. Example: include the module-level count function in native_transforms.
INPUT_INVALID_JSON: Input is not valid JSON. Fix: supply one JSON object, an array of objects, or newline-delimited JSON objects. Example: [{"value":12},{"value":15}]
INPUT_INVALID_NDJSON: One or more nonblank NDJSON lines is not a valid JSON object. Fix: put exactly one object on each line. Example: {"value":12} followed by a newline and {"value":15}.
INPUT_DUPLICATE_KEY: A JSON object contains a repeated property name; accepting it could change query meaning. Fix: retain only one occurrence of each key. Example: {"value":12}, not {"value":12,"value":15}.
INPUT_UNSUPPORTED_ROOT: The input root is not an object or an array of objects. Fix: wrap each scalar inside an object. Example: [{"value":12},{"value":15}] instead of [12,15].
INPUT_INVALID_UTF8: Input contains invalid UTF-8 encoding. Fix: encode the JSON text as UTF-8 without invalid byte sequences. Example: json.dumps(records, ensure_ascii=False).encode('utf-8').
INPUT_INVALID_NUMBER: Input contains a non-JSON or non-finite number. Fix: use finite JSON numbers and null for absent measurements. Example: {"value":null} rather than NaN or Infinity.
INPUT_TOO_DEEP: Input JSON nesting exceeds the configured limit. Fix: flatten or select a smaller object hierarchy before ingestion. Example: {"meta":{"kind":"a"}}.
INPUT_TOO_WIDE: Input contains more distinct field paths than the configured limit. Fix: project needed fields before ingestion or split the dataset into authorized smaller snapshots. Example: retain /time, /region and /value.
INPUT_RECORD_TOO_LARGE: A single JSON record exceeds the configured record-size limit. Fix: remove oversized free-text/binary payloads or split the record. Example: keep the numeric measurements rather than embedded document bodies.
INPUT_BYTES_LIMIT: Input payload exceeds the configured byte limit. Fix: submit fewer records or provide a trusted server-side data source. Example: register 10000 records instead of a multi-gigabyte MCP argument.
INPUT_ROWS_LIMIT: Input has more records than the configured admission limit. Fix: reduce the batch or use a trusted server-side adapter with approved chunking. Example: register a smaller time-bounded snapshot.
DATA_FIELD_UNKNOWN: The requested JSON Pointer does not appear in the authorized discovered schema. Fix: call analytics_describe, then use an exact listed path. Example: /metrics/latency rather than /metric/latency.
DATA_FIELD_TYPE_CONFLICT: A field contains incompatible JSON types and cannot be used directly by this operation. Fix: select a compatible field or add an explicit permitted cast. Example: casts:[{"field":"/value","to":"float64","on_error":"null"}].
DATA_FIELD_NOT_SCALAR: An operation requires a scalar field but the selected path contains an object or array. Fix: choose a scalar JSON Pointer inside the object. Example: /metrics/latency, not /metrics.
DATA_CAST_UNSUPPORTED: The requested type cast or timestamp format is not supported. Fix: use float64, int64, string or datetime with a documented format. Example: {"field":"/ts","to":"datetime","format":"rfc3339","on_error":"reject"}.
DATA_CAST_FAILED: One or more present values cannot be converted using the declared cast. Fix: correct the records or choose on_error=null if policy permits. Example: replace {"value":"unknown"} with a number before casting to float64.
DATA_TIMESTAMP_INVALID: The selected time field has an invalid or offset-ambiguous timestamp. Fix: use RFC3339 with Z or an explicit UTC offset, or declare a numeric epoch unit. Example: 2026-11-06T10:00:00Z.
QUERY_VERSION_UNSUPPORTED: The query language version is not supported. Fix: call analytics_capabilities and use a listed version. Example: "version":"analytics.query/v1".
QUERY_MALFORMED: The query object does not match the versioned contract, contains unknown properties, or has invalid data types. Fix: compare the request with the published schema. Example: use numeric "limit":100 rather than "limit":"100".
QUERY_UNKNOWN_OPERATOR: A filter, aggregation, or window operator is unsupported. Fix: select an operator listed by analytics_capabilities. Example: {"op":"p95","field":"/value","as":"p95_value"}.
QUERY_OPERATOR_TYPE: The selected operator cannot be applied to the field's resolved type. Fix: select a compatible field/operator or an approved explicit cast. Example: use avg on numeric /value rather than a string /label.
QUERY_INVALID_POINTER: A field path is not a valid RFC 6901 JSON Pointer. Fix: use slash-separated tokens and escape ~ as ~0 and / as ~1. Example: /metrics/latency.
QUERY_INVALID_LITERAL: A comparison value or membership list has an incompatible type, size, or shape. Fix: use a single typed scalar or a bounded homogeneous values list. Example: {"field":"/region","op":"in","values":["west","east"]}.
QUERY_PREDICATE_LIMIT: Predicate nesting or condition count exceeds V1 limits. Fix: simplify the AND/OR tree and split unrelated investigations into separate queries. Example: one AND with two comparisons.
QUERY_ALIAS_INVALID: An output alias is invalid, reserved, or duplicates another alias. Fix: use a unique identifier starting with a letter and containing only letters, digits or underscores. Example: "as":"avg_value".
QUERY_GROUP_INVALID: A group-by field is absent, incompatible, duplicated, or exceeds allowed grouping dimensions. Fix: group by a small number of visible scalar fields. Example: group_by:[{"field":"/region","as":"region"}].
QUERY_TIME_RANGE_INVALID: The time range is missing required boundaries, has an invalid timezone, or has start at/after end. Fix: use one relative range or offset-aware start and end. Example: {"field":"/ts","last_minutes":60}.
QUERY_WINDOW_INVALID: The time window has an invalid size, step, overlap, or missing time_range. Fix: use allowed fixed durations, with step not exceeding size. Example: {"type":"sliding","size":"5m","step":"1m"} with a valid time_range.
QUERY_EMPTY_WINDOW_UNSUPPORTED: Empty-window materialization is not supported for this unbounded or unconstrained group space. Fix: disable include_empty_windows or use a constrained small group set. Example: options:{"include_empty_windows":false}.
QUERY_HAVING_INVALID: A HAVING condition refers to an unavailable result alias or unsupported predicate. Fix: use an alias created by an aggregation or group_by. Example: having:[{"field":"events","op":"gte","value":2}].
QUERY_ORDER_INVALID: Order-by refers to an unknown result field or unsupported direction. Fix: sort by a declared alias or window_start/window_end. Example: order_by:[{"field":"events","direction":"desc"}].
QUERY_LIMIT_INVALID: The requested result limit is outside the configured range. Fix: use a positive integer within server limits. Example: "limit":100.
QUERY_UNSUPPORTED_FEATURE: The request uses a capability reserved for a future version, such as joins, unions, continuous queries, or external sinks. Fix: make a V1 single-dataset snapshot query. Example: dataset: {name: observations} without sources/joins/outputs.
QUERY_TOO_EXPENSIVE: The estimated query amplification, grouping cost, or data access exceeds the allowed budget. Fix: shorten the time range, reduce grouping dimensions, or increase the window step. Example: use a tumbling 5m window instead of many overlapping 1s windows.
ACCESS_DENIED: The caller is not authorized to perform this operation or to access this dataset or metadata. Fix: use a dataset registered under your authenticated session or request permission from its owner. Example: query a name discovered in your authenticated context.
ACCESS_FIELD_DENIED: A requested field or field metadata is restricted for this caller. Fix: query only fields returned by your authorized analytics_describe response. Example: remove a restricted group_by or aggregation path.
ACCESS_UPLOAD_DISABLED: This deployment does not permit agents to upload raw JSON through MCP. Fix: ask the trusted hosting application to register records using the Python SDK and provide a context-local logical name. Example: engine.register_records(name="observations", records=records).
RESOURCE_GROUPS_LIMIT: The number of distinct groups exceeds the execution budget. Fix: remove high-cardinality group_by fields or filter to a smaller scope. Example: group by /region instead of /request_id.
RESOURCE_WINDOWS_LIMIT: The number of generated temporal windows exceeds the limit. Fix: choose a larger step/size or reduce the time range. Example: size=5m and step=5m instead of size=1h and step=1s.
RESOURCE_RESULT_LIMIT: The serialized result exceeds the permitted byte or row budget. Fix: reduce limit, group cardinality, or requested output fields. Example: set limit=50 and rank by a numeric aggregate.
RESOURCE_MEMORY_LIMIT: An execution exceeded its allocated memory budget. Fix: reduce input size or query complexity and retry once if permitted. Example: aggregate a smaller authorized snapshot.
RESOURCE_TIMEOUT: An analytical query exceeded its execution deadline. Fix: use a smaller snapshot, narrower range or fewer groups, then retry. Example: remove an expensive count_distinct on a high-cardinality field.
RESOURCE_CONCURRENCY_LIMIT: The caller reached the allowed concurrent query count. Fix: finish or cancel an existing request and retry after backoff. Example: run one analytics_query at a time for the same dataset.
EXECUTION_CANCELLED: The execution was canceled before completion. Fix: re-run the query only if the caller still needs it and the same logical dataset binding is valid. Example: submit the original query after an explicit cancellation acknowledgment.
EXECUTION_BACKEND_ERROR: The analytical backend could not complete the requested operation. Fix: verify the query with analytics_validate_query and retry only if permitted; report the query_id if the failure persists. Example: rerun with a supported aggregation such as avg.
MCP_INVALID_TOOL_CALL: The MCP tool arguments or invocation shape are invalid. Fix: list the available tools and follow the published tool input schema. Example: call analytics_describe(name="observations").
MCP_UNAVAILABLE: The MCP adapter or selected transport is unavailable. Fix: reconnect and verify the server and transport configuration. Example: start the server using the documented xp-libs-analytics entry point.
INTERNAL_ERROR: An unexpected server error occurred; no record data is included in this message. Fix: report the query_id to the operator and avoid blind repeated retries. Example: check the server's trace for that query_id.
QUERY_YAML_INVALID:
The YAML query contains a syntax or indentation error. Fix: submit one correctly indented YAML mapping and quote ambiguous strings. Example: aggregations:
  - op: count
    as: rows.
QUERY_YAML_DUPLICATE_KEY: The YAML query repeats a mapping key, so its meaning is ambiguous. Fix: keep exactly one occurrence of the key at that mapping level. Example: limit: 100 appears once, not twice.
QUERY_YAML_ANCHOR_FORBIDDEN: YAML anchors are not supported in analytical queries. Fix: write each bounded filter or aggregation explicitly without &anchor. Example: aggregations: [{op: count, as: rows}].
QUERY_YAML_ALIAS_FORBIDDEN: YAML aliases are not supported because they can create recursive or amplified document graphs. Fix: expand the intended bounded mapping explicitly without *alias. Example: filters: [{field: /region, op: eq, value: west}].
QUERY_YAML_TAG_FORBIDDEN: Explicit YAML tags and tag directives are not supported. Fix: use ordinary mappings, sequences and scalar values; never use ! or !! constructors. Example: limit: 100.
QUERY_YAML_MULTI_DOCUMENT: Only one YAML query document may be submitted at a time. Fix: remove additional document separators and send one root mapping. Example: version: analytics.query/v1 followed by dataset and aggregations in the same document.
QUERY_YAML_ROOT_INVALID: A YAML query must be a nonempty mapping with string keys. Fix: put version, dataset, and aggregations under one top-level mapping. Example: version: analytics.query/v1.
QUERY_YAML_COMPLEXITY_LIMIT: The YAML query exceeds permitted bytes, nesting, nodes, keys or scalar length. Fix: simplify predicates or split the investigation into separate bounded queries. Example: a single filter with two conditions.
QUERY_YAML_SCALAR_INVALID: The YAML query contains an unsupported or non-finite scalar representation. Fix: use finite decimal numbers or quote data intended as text. Example: value: 12.5 instead of value: .nan.
DATASET_NAME_UNKNOWN: Dataset name is not registered in this context. Fix: discover available names with analytics_list_datasets. Example: dataset: {name: observations}.
DATASET_NAME_DUPLICATE: Dataset name is already registered in this context. Fix: choose a different name or use replace_records to publish a new snapshot. Example: replace_records("observations", records).
DATASET_NAME_INVALID: Dataset name is invalid. Fix: use 1 to 64 ASCII letters, digits, underscores or hyphens, starting with a letter. Example: observations_2026.
DATASET_SNAPSHOT_STALE: Dataset snapshot has expired or its revision no longer matches. Fix: discover current metadata and publish or reference the current snapshot. Example: describe("observations").
RESOURCE_DATASETS_LIMIT: Named dataset budget exceeded. Fix: unregister an unused dataset before registering another. Example: unregister_dataset("observations").
MATCH_PATTERN_INVALID: String pattern is invalid. Fix: escape only percent, underscore or backslash in LIKE, and use nonempty bounded search values. Example: {field: /text, op: like, value: "Pet%"}.
MATCH_REGEX_INVALID: Regex is not supported by the Rust engine. Fix: remove lookaround/backreferences or use literal matching. Example: {field: /text, op: regex, value: "^Pet[a-z]+$"}.
MATCH_REGEX_POLICY: Regex or wildcard pattern exceeds host policy or is an empty-string catch-all. Fix: use a bounded selective pattern without unsupported flags. Example: {field: /text, op: contains, value: Peter}.
MATCH_NORMALIZATION_INVALID: String normalization is incompatible with this predicate or field. Fix: normalize strings only; regex permits case handling only, and ILIKE cannot request case-sensitive matching. Example: normalization: {case_sensitive: false, unicode: nfkc, trim: true}.
MATCH_FUZZY_ALGORITHM_INVALID: Fuzzy scorer is invalid or absent. Fix: choose an approved algorithm. Example: {field: /text, op: fuzzy, value: Peter, algorithm: ratio, min_score: 85}.
MATCH_FUZZY_THRESHOLD_INVALID: Fuzzy similarity threshold is invalid, absent or below host policy. Fix: supply a finite numeric min_score within the allowed range. Example: {field: /text, op: fuzzy, value: Peter, algorithm: ratio, min_score: 85}.
MATCH_FUZZY_QUERY_TOO_SHORT: Normalized fuzzy search text is shorter than host policy permits. Fix: provide longer text or use exact/literal matching. Example: {field: /text, op: eq, value: Li}.
MATCH_CANDIDATE_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: Exhaustive string matching exceeds the host candidate, length or byte budget. Fix: narrow authorized time/nonfuzzy filters without claiming a complete result for the original scope. Example: filters: [{field: /status, op: eq, value: error}].
MATCH_COMPLEXITY_BUDGET_EXCEEDED: Matching fields, patterns or total comparisons exceed host policy. Fix: reduce repeated matching work or narrow eligible data; result limit does not reduce scanning. Example: match: {fields: [/text], patterns: [{op: word, value: Peter}], mode: any}.
MATCH_DIAGNOSTICS_UNAUTHORIZED: Raw matching values are not authorized by host and field disclosure policy. Fix: request redacted diagnostics. Example: options: {matching_details: {include: true, include_raw_values: false}}.
MATCH_ENTITY_INFERENCE_UNSUPPORTED: V1 string similarity does not resolve or verify identities, aliases or entity ownership. Fix: report matching observed values without merging people. Example: {field: /text, op: fuzzy, value: Peter, algorithm: ratio, min_score: 85}.
